correctness.rationale: Explicit monotone odometer comparison against the maximal stable configuration proves an all-vertices-once upper bound for all stable inputs. Maximal event implies t initially at its threshold and every remaining B vertex nonzero; subtract one on those vertices to obtain an auxiliary recurrent state on \\(K_{a-1,b}\\) rooted t. Conversely forbidden-subconfiguration recurrence and the burning criterion give a bijection. Matrix-tree counts yield exact probability. Averaged Laplacian equations under recurrent-state stationarity yield the exact mean. Two independent standard-library scripts fully enumerate ten finite graph sizes, compare counts and exact rational Green functions; no finite check is used in place of the general proof.

value.rationale: An exact infinite-family classification of largest system-spanning driven avalanches gives its probability, finite count, structural deleted-graph correspondence, and exact expected-activity share. In the balanced family the maximal event is rare with probability order \\(1/n\\) but accounts for asymptotically \\(e^{-1}\\) of mean activity, a motivated physical rare-event statistic not determined by the number of recurrent states alone. It is more than a normalization or routine finite census.
